acts.title: Text A · Why gold, of all things
text: Gold has held human attention for one reason above all others: there is almost none of it. Every gram ever mined would fit into a cube about twenty-two metres on each side, which is roughly the size of a small office building.

Its second quality is that it does not change. Iron rusts, silver blackens, and copper turns green, but a gold coin buried for two thousand years comes out of the ground looking exactly as it went in.

Its third quality is the one nobody expects: it is enormously useful. A multitude of modern devices depend on it, because it conducts electricity well and does not corrode. There are about thirty milligrams of gold in a mobile phone.
Scarcity, permanence and usefulness are an unusual combination, and no other metal has all three. That, rather than the colour, is the significance of gold.

items.q: Skim the text. What is it mainly about?
o: The three qualities that make gold unusual

items.q: Which sentence in paragraph two carries the paragraph?
o: Its second quality is that it does not change.
A gold coin buried for two thousand years…

acts.title: Text B · Why most goals fail
text: Most goals fail because they cannot be measured. “Get fitter” has no finishing line, so there is never a day on which you have done it, and there is never a day on which you have obviously not.

The second reason is that people overestimate the day and underestimate the year. They set a goal that would require four hours a day, run it for a fortnight, and conclude that they lack discipline rather than that the plan was wrong.

The third reason is relevance. A goal borrowed from somebody else survives contact with a bad week for about three days. If you cannot say why it matters to you specifically, the answer is usually that it does not.
Measurable, realistic, relevant. It is not an inspiring list, and it is the whole of the difference between an achievement and an intention.

items.s: The writer says “get fitter” is a poor goal because it cannot be measured.
People generally underestimate what they can do in a single day.
A borrowed goal, according to the text, survives a bad week easily.
The writer names three reasons goals fail.
The writer thinks the three-item list is inspiring.

acts.title: Turning verbs and adjectives into nouns
rule: Academic and professional English is noun-heavy. Being able to build the noun from a verb or an adjective is worth more at B2 than learning the noun separately, because the suffix is predictable far more often than not.
points: From verbs, usually about an action or its result: achieve → achievement, adjust → adjustment, enjoy → enjoyment.
From verbs, the largest group by far: invite → invitation, decide → decision, civilize → civilization.
From adjectives, about a quality: happy → happiness, dark → darkness, willing → willingness.
From adjectives, often ending -al, -able or -ous: flexible → flexibility, generous → generosity, able → ability.
From verbs and adjectives, and unpredictable between the two: prefer → preference, relevant → relevance, significant → significance.
acts.careful: The stress often moves when the suffix is added. preFER becomes PREference; SIGnify becomes signIFicance. If you learn the noun without the stress, you will be understood on paper and not in speech.

write.q: Write four paragraphs of about 45 words each on a subject you know well, and make the first sentence of every paragraph carry the whole paragraph. Then, underneath, write your four topic sentences on their own and check that they alone tell the reader what the piece says. Use at least four nouns built with the suffixes from this lesson.
plan: four paragraphs, each opening with its main idea
the four topic sentences alone underneath
check they make sense on their own
write.model:
Most sales training fails for the same reason most diets do: it changes behaviour for a fortnight. The enthusiasm is real, the improvement is measurable for about ten days, and then the old habits return, because nothing around the person changed.

The second problem is relevance. A course written for a different market, a different price point and a different length of sales cycle will be politely received and quietly ignored.

The third is measurement. If nobody defines what improvement looks like, there is no achievement to point at afterwards, and no way to tell a good week from a lucky one.

What works is smaller and duller: one specific change, measured weekly, with the manager in the room.

TOPIC SENTENCES
1. Most sales training fails because it changes behaviour for a fortnight.
2. The second problem is relevance.
3. The third is measurement.
4. What works is smaller and duller.
